archetypes.pitch: Small folk, big numbers. A flood of Kithkin and tokens turns Kinbinding into a growing anthem, and Brigid, Clachan's Heart pays you for every creature that turned up this turn. Pick this if you want a board that gets wider and taller at the same time.
archetypes.rationale: 21 typed Kithkin plus a token flood, backed by an untagged 'a creature entered this turn' payoff suite (Crossroads Watcher, Bristlebane Outrider, Thoughtweft Charge) that Kinbinding scales into an anthem.

archetypes.pitch: Your creatures pay for your spells and then get paid for it. Convoke taps the school to cast, which is exactly what Sygg, Wanderwine Wisdom and the tap-triggers were waiting for, while Adept Watershaper makes a fully tapped board indestructible. For players who like tempo decks that never really tap out.
archetypes.rationale: Five 'whenever this creature becomes tapped' payoffs plus 16 convoke cards as tap outlets, with Deepway Navigator and Deepchannel Duelist untapping and Adept Watershaper making the tapped board indestructible.

archetypes.pitch: The deepest tribe in the cube, pointed straight at the opponent's face. Every Elemental that enters pings in for Champion of the Path, Ashling, Rekindled keeps the fire coming, and Twinflame Travelers doubles the triggers outright. Pick this if you want your late game to be damage rather than a board.
archetypes.rationale: The cube's deepest tribe at 34 Elementals, layered over five 'mana value 4 or greater' triggers, with Twinflame Travelers doubling Elemental triggers and Flamebraider/Sunderflock making the top end castable.

archetypes.pitch: A swarm of Boggarts worth more dead than alive. Boggart Cursecrafter and Grub, Storied Matriarch drain a little every time a Goblin dies, and blight counters let you finish off your own tokens on demand. Pick this if you like a deck where chump-blocking is a resource rather than a concession.
archetypes.rationale: 23 Goblins with two repeatable 'whenever a Goblin you control dies' drains, fed by token makers and by untagged death triggers on Mudbutton Cursetosser and Bile-Vial Boggart.

archetypes.pitch: Elves that count the ones already buried. Morcant's Eyes and its fellow payoffs grow with every Elf in the yard, so self-mill becomes acceleration instead of a cost, and High Perfect Morcant turns that pile back into a board. For players who want a tribal deck with a second dimension.
archetypes.rationale: 29 Elves whose payoffs count Elf cards in the graveyard, not just on board (Gloom Ripper, Morcant's Eyes, Lys Alana Dignitary, Creakwood Safewright), turning the self-mill suite into an enabler.

archetypes.pitch: Almost nothing you do happens on your own turn. Flash bodies and counterspells hold the game open while Voracious Tome-Skimmer and Bitterbloom Bearer pay you for every spell cast during an opponent's turn. Pick this if you enjoy playing draw-go and somehow still building a board.
archetypes.rationale: Three 'whenever you cast a spell during an opponent's turn' payoffs supported by 16 flash cards and four counterspells; Illusion Spinners earns its slot from 'cast as though it had flash if you control a Faerie'.

archetypes.pitch: The set's signature mechanic sells you oversized creatures at a discount, then asks you to manage the debt. Shadow Urchin turns every -1/-1 counter into value and Lasting Tarfire spends them as removal. For players who like a deck where the drawback is the engine.
archetypes.rationale: The set's signature mechanic and largest non-tribal cluster: 16 undercosted creatures enter with -1/-1 counters, shedding engines remove them, and 25 cards use blight as a cost; Shadow Urchin and Lasting Tarfire are the standalone payoffs.

archetypes.pitch: Small creatures that refuse to stay dead, and a life total that keeps climbing. Isilu, Carrier of Twilight hands persist to the rest of the team while Reaping Willow and Emptiness rebuy whatever dies anyway. Pick this if you want to win a long attrition war without ever casting an expensive card.
archetypes.rationale: Four capped reanimation effects (MV 3 or less / power 2 or less) plus Isilu granting every other nontoken creature persist; 23 lifegain cards feed Bre of Clan Stoutarm's 'if you gained life this turn' card advantage.

archetypes.pitch: Enormous bodies bought cheap, paid for with -1/-1 counters you were glad to spend. Boldwyr Aggressor hands the tribe double strike and Hovel Hurler turns the leftover counters into reach. Pick this if you want to cast things far above the curve and start swinging immediately.
archetypes.rationale: 11 Giants built as blighted oversized bodies that spend their -1/-1 counters on activated abilities; Boldwyr Aggressor grants the tribe double strike and Pummeler for Hire scales off 'the greatest power among Giants you control'.

archetypes.pitch: A deck where every extra colour on the battlefield makes your cards bigger. Bloom Tender and a pile of duals stretch you to four or five colours, and Prismatic Undercurrents and Aurora Awakener scale directly off that count. For players who enjoy a greedy mana base that actually pays out.
archetypes.rationale: 14 Vivid cards all key off 'the number of colors among permanents you control', supported by 15 dual lands and eight other fixers; Tam and Puca's Eye inflate the colour count directly without carrying a Domain tag.

archetypes.pitch: Mana first, questions later. Treasures, dorks and Vibrance put you turns ahead of schedule, Aurora Awakener cashes that in for a board, and Raiding Schemes gives your noncreature spells conspire so a wide board doubles them. Pick this if you like turns that visibly snowball.
archetypes.rationale: Five Treasure makers plus dorks, Shimmerwilds Growth and Lavaleaper build the mana; Raiding Schemes is the distinguishing payoff, giving every noncreature spell conspire so a wide board doubles removal and draw.

archetypes.pitch: Mill yourself, then take it all back at once. Most of the recursion here is small and cheap, but Bloodline Bidding returns an entire creature type from the yard and Twilight Diviner keeps the pile stocked. For players who would rather play from the graveyard than from hand.
archetypes.rationale: 14 mill/surveil cards feed six reanimation and ten graveyard-to-hand effects; every reanimation is capped small except Bloodline Bidding, which mass-returns one creature type and so only a tribal self-mill deck can aim it.

archetypes.pitch: Every creature is every creature. Changelings switch on behold costs and choose-a-type cards in any deck, so Gathering Stone and Chronicle of Victory always have a target and Collective Inferno only ever kills their half of the board. Pick this if you like decks built out of rules text.
archetypes.rationale: 18 changelings make the 11 'choose a creature type' cards and 12 behold costs live in any deck; Winnowing becomes a one-sided wrath because a changeling shares a type with everything you keep.

archetypes.pitch: Your board is your mana. Tokens flood in, convoke turns them into spells you should not be able to cast yet, and Eirdu, Carrier of Dawn hands convoke to your creature spells as well. Pick this if you like curving out and then casting something enormous several turns early.
archetypes.rationale: 16 convoke cards alongside 40 token-generation effects, extended by Eirdu's 'creature spells you cast have convoke'; tapping as a cost overlaps directly with the tapped-matters payoffs, High Perfect Morcant and Kirol.

archetypes.pitch: Creatures that block all day and then hit like trucks. Doran, Besieged by Time makes everything deal damage equal to its toughness, turning the cube's butt-heavy bodies into real threats, and Bark of Doran spreads the trick around. For players who like a defence that turns lethal without warning.
archetypes.rationale: Only 7 typed Treefolk, so this is Doran's deck: he discounts toughness-heavy creature spells and pumps them by the power/toughness gap, which the cube's butt-heavy untagged bodies (3/7, 0/5, 2/5, 5/6) turn on.

archetypes.pitch: Make one good thing, then make several more of it. Mirrormind Crown turns each turn's first batch of tokens into copies of your best creature, and Mirrorform duplicates anything else worth having twice. Pick this if you enjoy assembling a two-card engine that makes a 1/1 maker win the game.
archetypes.rationale: Mirrormind Crown converts every 1/1 token maker in the cube into copies of your best creature; 13 copy effects exist but sit in four colours with no shared enabler, so it is assembled rather than drafted open.

archetypes.pitch: One creature, fully kitted out, swinging alone. Lofty Dreams and Stalactite Dagger stack the stats while flash protection Auras double as combat tricks, so your threat survives the removal aimed at it. For players who enjoy the tension of putting everything on a single body.
archetypes.rationale: 13 Auras and Equipment, de-risked by flash-and-protection Auras that double as combat tricks; Evershrike's Gift buys itself back for '{1}{W}, Blight 2', tying it to the blight package. Thin on payoffs beyond raw stats.

archetypes.pitch: Green ramp where every land drop is progress. Sapling Nursery is the cube's one true landfall payoff, fetches and landcycling keep the triggers coming, and Prismatic Undercurrents scales off the duals you were already playing. Pick this if you want a grindy green deck built out of its mana base.
archetypes.rationale: Only two true Landfall cards, both green and both strong, with incidental fetch density (Evolving Wilds, Tend the Sprigs, two basic-landcycling creatures) rather than a dedicated enabler suite.

archetypes.pitch: Play off the top of your library instead of out of your hand. Exile-and-cast effects turn spare mana into extra cards, and Goliath Daydreamer recasts your used instants and sorceries free on every attack. For players who like grinding out extra cards while still attacking every single turn.
archetypes.rationale: Seven cards exile from the top of a library and let you play those cards later; Goliath Daydreamer is the only piece that compounds, recasting your used instants and sorceries free on each attack.

archetypes.pitch: A lock built out of one card. Mornsong Aria turns every draw step into a tutor and a three-life clock, and you break the symmetry with hand attack and graveyard denial. Pick this if you want the strangest, meanest deck in the cube and do not mind drawing fewer cards yourself.
archetypes.rationale: A true single-card anchor - the cube's only Stax/Taxing card - turning every draw step into a tutor and a 3-life clock; you break the symmetry with hand attack and graveyard denial, at the cost of your own draw and lifegain.
